heroText: Caracas is Venezuela's mountain-framed capital, set below Avila National Park with grand civic spaces, museums and sharp contrasts between neighborhoods. Use Chacao or Altamira as a practical base, visit Plaza Bolivar and the Museo de Bellas Artes by day, then plan Waraira Repano or Galipan with local advice. Maiquetia airport is on the coast, so transfers require care and timing.

areas.text: Chacao is one of the most practical visitor bases, with restaurants, hotels, offices and better evening logistics than central areas.

areas.name: La Castellana

areas.name: Sabana Grande

travelTips.title: Safety first
travelTips.text: Use current local advice, arranged transfers and trusted taxis; avoid displaying phones, jewelry or cameras in public.

travelTips.title: Best base
travelTips.text: Choose Chacao or Altamira for a first stay because hotels, restaurants and transport logistics are more manageable.

travelTips.title: Airport transfers
travelTips.text: Pre-arrange Maiquetia transfers through a hotel or trusted operator, especially for late arrivals or early departures.

travelTips.title: Mountain plans
travelTips.text: Visit Avila or Galipan with clear weather, local guidance and enough daylight for the return journey.

history.text: Francisco Fajardo, the son of a Spanish captain and a Guaiqueri cacica, who came from Margarita, began establishing settlements in the area of La Guaira and the Caracas valley between 1555 and 1560.
Fajardo's 1560 settlement was known as Hato de San Francisco, and another attempt in 1561 by Juan Rodríguez de Suárez was called Villa de San Francisco, and was also destroyed by the same native.

Before the city was founded in 1567, the valley of Caracas was populated by indigenous peoples.
